summary.name: Balsamiq
summary.one_liner: Balsamiq is a browser-based, low-fidelity wireframing and clickable prototyping tool for product teams, with AI drafting and an MCP server for connecting boards to AI coding tools.
use_cases: sketching early product ideas before building
wireframing new screens or user flows
creating clickable prototypes to test with users
aligning stakeholders on requirements in reviews
handing off validated designs to engineers
summary.what_it_does: Balsamiq lets you build editable, intentionally low-fidelity wireframes from a component library, or by describing a screen or dropping in a screenshot or sketch to Balsamiq AI. It can generate a clickable prototype from selected screens, which the page says takes about a minute. Teams can share a link and collect comments and reactions directly on the board. Boards can be embedded in Jira, Confluence, and Notion, and exported to PNG, PDF, or HTML. The page also describes an MCP server that lets Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and other MCP-compatible tools read and edit Balsamiq projects.
notable: Low-fidelity by design, so discussions focus on the idea rather than visual polish
Balsamiq AI drafts wireframes from text, screenshots, or sketches
MCP server connects boards to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and similar tools
Runs in the browser with nothing to install
caveats: Pricing and free-tier details are not stated on this page
The page is mostly marketing; claims about speed and AI results are unverified
Figma, Miro and Whimsical comparisons are the vendor's own framing
